title: Bound on Nested-Loop Cost
statement: Let $q,C\in\mathbb{N}$ with $q>0$, and let $\kappa_{q,C}$ be defined by $\kappa_{q,C}(0)=C+1$ and $\kappa_{q,C}(r+1)=q(\kappa_{q,C}(r)+2)+q+2$. Then, for every $r\in\mathbb{N}$, $\kappa_{q,C}(r)\le (C+1+5r)q^r$.
replaced: Let $q, C \in \mathbb{N}$ with $q > 0$, and let $\kappa_{q,C} \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be given by $\kappa_{q,C}(0) = C + 1$ and $\kappa_{q,C}(r+1) = q(\kappa_{q,C}(r) + 2) + q + 2$. Then $\kappa_{q,C}(r) \le (C + 1 + 5r)\,q^r$ for every $r \in \mathbb{N}$.
